integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A single continuous fifteen-second LIVE-ACTION shot, animating the EXACT approved older theatre impresario in this image, with one real human actor. Preserve his face, receding grey hair, thick curved grey moustache, portly proportions, dark NAVY BLUE frock coat, ivory waistcoat and white cravat, dark trousers and worn leather shoes. This is the same physical side-curtain set in the supplied photograph: burgundy velvet, timber rigging and ropes at the sides, small candle table at left, wooden floor and side chair. Preserve these practical objects, natural skin and textile colours. He holds the SAME single folded handwritten letter already shown; do not introduce a baton, instrument, book, flowers, weapon or another actor. Keep the main velvet curtain opaque and closed throughout. Camera remains fixed at its supplied full-body viewpoint; his shoes, floor contacts and full head remain visible. Gentle steady warm theatrical light, neutral natural skin, dark navy cloth and ivory waistcoat, stable exposure with no pink or magenta wash.

From0-3.5s the impresario wants to be ready to introduce the performance. He shifts his eyes down from the offscreen stage cue to the letter, brings the same paper slightly closer with BOTH normal hands and reads it silently. His mouth stays at rest, no articulated syllables, singing or speaking. A single small concerned breath raises his chest and then settles; do not repeat blinking, nodding or swaying. Feet are supported on the wooden floor and his head follows the downward eye direction without changing his face.

From3.5-7.5s he hears the music settle into the next phrase, lifts his eyes toward the audience beyond the camera slightly to his right, then lowers the intact letter to waist level. His right hand keeps hold of the paper edge and his left hand releases it naturally, relaxes at his side. The paper retains its same dimensions, folded edges and colour; it is never torn, duplicated, transformed or pocketed. He straightens his posture with a visible weight transfer onto the left foot in preparation to advance. His lips remain at rest; there is no recorded sung part to perform here.

From7.5-11.5s the impresario commits to the introduction: he takes TWO SMALL measured forward steps toward the audience, first right foot and then left, with genuine heel-to-toe floor contact, knee and hip flexion and body weight arriving after each foot. He advances less than one shoe length per step so the entire body stays inside this same framing. His right arm carries the same letter low beside his right hip, away from his face. Coat tails respond subtly after the body, no fabric morph or sliding feet. He does not pass through the curtain, table, chair or any rope. The camera and set stay fixed, the curtain remains an opaque stationary backdrop.

From11.5-15.08s he stops securely on both feet, looks toward the waiting audience and makes ONE restrained formal acknowledgement: a shallow inclination from the waist and head followed by a natural controlled return upright. The letter remains held low in his right hand. His left hand opens in a small welcoming gesture at waist height and then relaxes. He is ready for the introduction, attentive and dignified rather than frozen. Keep his mouth resting CLOSED, no mouthing words, fake lip-sync or singing. Leave him upright, listening and physically supported at the final frame. Only this one named impresario is present. No title, text, new character, applause, flash, fade, scenic moon, castle or curtain reveal.
